# Poem

![](images/taker_of_thoughts_symbol.png){style="width:300px" fig-align="center"}

The below poem was found within a printed book of poetry by a Caroline Gurnsey.
Caroline Gurnsey was found dead of dehydration at a writing desk in a forgotten house.

She was surrounded by other printed books of her, all with valid but unused ISBN ids.
Seemingly a prolific writer yet no one remembers her.

A copy of her book "Reclamations and forfeits" was open on the below poem.
The last stanza, not in the original print, was written with quill and ink.
Many other copies were strewn across the flow, open on the poem with the last stanza manually added too.

## The Taker of Thoughts {.h2centre}

<center>
> Grab its white feather,<br>
> Write with its thick ink.<br>
> Surrender your words till you're not but leather,<br>
> Then with empty brain you can let your head sink.
>
> Lay it atop a down pillow,<br>
> And descend to the abyss.<br>
> Every thought weighs a kilo,<br>
> so write them down as a list.
>
> Body of a plucked goose,<br>
> Head of a dried squid.<br>
> Our success is just a ruse,<br>
> For it'll win with its black liquid.
>
> For to enchant others the payment’s your mind,<br>
> To be replaced with its inkened blots.<br>
> So be content with your fate assigned,<br>
> Decided upon by the taker of thoughts.
>
::: {.tot}
> Who wrote this poem?<br>
> It's in my hand.<br>
> Did it come from my dome?<br>
> I don't understand.
:::
</center>
